summary: Background token renewal race leads to idempotency-scope mismatch and duplicate function/tool invocations
description:
Issue summary: ParcelWise is seeing duplicated external side effects (webhook-triggered downstream jobs and duplicate DB writes) when their clients use the Python SDK and the client library performs a background API token refresh while the SDK is retrying a failed funcall. Impact: intermittent duplicate tool/function invocations observed ~0.5-1% of requests for a specific customer fleet; customer reports material downstream cost and correctness issues for financial reconciliation jobs.

High-level observed behavior: the SDK generates an idempotency key derived from a short-lived session token plus request fingerprint. When the token auto-renews mid-retry, the derived idempotency key changes for the retry attempt and the server treats it as a distinct request. The funcall runs twice: first attempt may have succeeded but callback or confirmation didn't reach client before retry; second attempt executes and causes duplicate webhook payloads.

Why this ticket: customer asks for guidance and a mitigation path that fits their Dedicated deployment and their requirement that long-running orchestration tasks remain exactly-once when possible.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer using python-sdk v2.7.1 with default token refresh configured (background refresh window = 30s).
2) Create a long-running funcall that triggers an external webhook side-effect (simulate downstream job submission).
3) Force a transient 503 on the funcall request (eg. temporarily route through a proxy that returns 503 once).
4) Allow the SDK to perform an automatic retry while the client's session token expires and background-refresh runs concurrently, producing a new access token mid-retry.
5) Observe two webhook deliveries within a short window and two server-side funcall execution traces with different idempotency keys but identical payloads/request fingerprint.
observed_logs: 2026-03-10T11:22:05Z INFO serving-runtime:exec funcall_id=fc-98765 model=redwood-tooling-funcall-v1 status=executed idempotency_key=HMACv1:tokenA:fp123
2026-03-10T11:22:06Z INFO serving-runtime:exec funcall_id=fc-98766 model=redwood-tooling-funcall-v1 status=executed idempotency_key=HMACv1:tokenB:fp123
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: idempotency key derivation in the customer SDK is session-token scoped, so token rotation mid-flight changes the computed key for the same logical request.

Confirmed with customer: python-sdk computes idempotency_key = HMAC(secret=session_token, message=request_fingerprint). The secret is replaced during background refresh without persisting original key mapping for in-flight retries.

Server behavior: Redwood API treats idempotency_key as opaque unique key. There is no built-in mapping from previous token-scoped keys to new token-scoped keys, so duplicate execution occurs when derived key changes.
We reproduced locally using SDK v2.7.1 and a proxy that enforces 503 on first attempt. Repro rate ~8/100 tries in local env when refresh window overlaps retry backoff window.
temporary_workaround: Customer-side: upgrade to patched helper (recommended below) or set SDK to use client-provided stable idempotency keys (explicit X-Idempotency-Key) that persist across token refresh events. Server-side: enable webhook deduplication for this project (best-effort) and add compensating logic in downstream to be idempotent to duplicate jobs.
recommendations_and_next_steps: Short term (immediate): instruct ParcelWise to switch to an explicit idempotency key for long-running funcalls. Provide code snippet and sample wrapper that persists a client-generated UUID per logical operation and uses it for retry attempts.

Medium term (SDK change): ship a python-sdk patch that computes a stable client-scoped idempotency key by default for up to 60s across token rotations (persist key in the request object), and expose a config flag keep_idempotency_across_refresh=true.
Longer term (platform): consider allowing the API to accept an alternate header X-Client-Op-Id to map token-scoped keys into a single logical idempotency namespace for dedicated/private tenants.
Engineering follow-up: create INT ticket for SDK patch and design doc (linked INT-4422). SRE to review server-side dedupe safeguards for webhook deliveries in dedicated clusters.

resolution: Workaround provided: customer set explicit stable idempotency keys for logical operations and enabled webhook dedupe on their dedicated webhook queue. Engineering accepted INT-4422 for SDK patch; target: add keep_idempotency_across_refresh flag in python-sdk v2.8.0 (ETA 2026-03-26). Ticket remains open until SDK patch is released and customer confirms resolution in production.
